title: Weekends in New Orleans: Fazola, the Jazz Club and Parisian Room
summary: As a pre-med student from Baton Rouge, Steinau tried to catch radio jazz, club meetings and Parisian Room concerts, hearing Irving Fazola and other white musicians.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: I was, I was 20 and 21, and I'm finishing my pre-med studies. And my family was in New Orleans. And I would try very hard, both to catch Roger Wolfe's jazz show on WDSU, which I think was on Friday nights, may have been Saturdays. And also, sometimes, to go to jazz club meetings. Because the New Orleans jazz club, I think, started in 47. Might have been 46, but it was around that time. There were a couple of abortive initial attempts. And also, to go to the Parisian Room concerts, which were down in the 100 block of Royal Street, in the building that, in a quite old building that had housed Gluck's, that was currently, at least at the time, housing Gluck's Restaurant and some other places. And the Parisian Room was a hall upstairs. And I remember some of the first people I heard there. Most particularly, I remember Irving Fazola, who was the one I'd heard most of. But a number of other musicians, including Sharky, Lester Bouchon, Chink Martin, Monk Hazel, Frank Federico. Those are the ones that come to mind. I'm particularly impressed with Fazola. who died, I think, within a year or two of that.

I think he died in 49. That was before, he died before I came to New Orleans in 49. In any case, but he'd been around for many, many years and in and out of town, of course, too. So he had a reputation. Yeah,
Well, there was a lot of other people, but that was the one
Crosby was the one I knew at that time. Yeah, where he was featured.
These were strictly lily-white bands. There wasn't a black musician in the bunch, but they, at times, played very well and very excitingly, and I enjoyed them all.
Perfect. That somehow reminds me of Lizzie Miles, who used to sing up there with Tony Almarico later. Did you ever hear her?
